parts.label: (i)
parts.answer: The discriminant is $(3k+1)^2\ge0$, so the curve and line meet for all $k$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: For their three-term quadratic, a recognisable application of $b^2-4ac$. — M1. Guidance: Expect $2x^2-x(3+k)+1-k^2(=0)$ oe for the three-term quadratic. $(b^2-4ac)=(3+k)^2-4(2)(1-k^2)$ oe. — A1. Guidance: Must be correct. Ignore any RHS. $9k^2+6k+1$. — A1. Guidance: Ignore any RHS. $(3k+1)^2\ge0$; do not allow $>0$. Hence curve and line meet. — A1 AG. Guidance: Allow $9(k+\frac13)^2\ge0$. Conclusion required. ALT: Attempt solution of three-term quadratic. — M1. Solutions $x=k+1$, $\frac12(1-k)$. — A1A1. These exist for all values of $k$. Hence curve and line meet. — A1 AG. Total 4.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: $k=-\frac13$. — B1. Guidance: ALT $\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=4x-3\Rightarrow4x-3=k$. Substitute one of their $k=-\frac13$ into either line: $2x^2-\frac83x+\frac89=0$, or into the derivative: $4x-(3+k)=0$. — M1. Guidance: Alternatively substitute $k=4x-3$ into line 1 $\to2x^2-x(4x)+1-(4x-3)^2=0$. $x=\frac23$. — A1. Guidance: Do not allow unsubstantiated $(\frac23,-\frac19)$ following $k=-\frac13$; both $x=\frac23,y=-\frac19$ required [from $-18x^2+24x-8=0$ oe]. $y=-\frac19$. — A1. Guidance: Do not allow unsubstantiated $(\frac23,-\frac19)$ following $k=-\frac13$. Total 4.
